page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, it provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 372.0 GB, providing 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. For hardware acceleration, the instance integrates four NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs supplying a combined 64 GB of VRAM. Networking features a 30 Gbps baseline bandwidth profile, and there is no included local storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded parallel compute capacity alongside weaker single-core processing. Single-core stress-ng tests yield a score of 1103.89 and single-threaded gzip compression measures 19.2 GB/sec, reflecting limited individual core performance. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng testing reaches 70574.45, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 287.37 GB/sec. Cached memory read throughput is measured at 3924.63 GB/sec, whereas uncached large block reads average 147.24 GB/sec. High-concurrency operations reach 64.27 million Redis SET operations per second.

The combination of 96 vCPUs and four NVIDIA T4 GPUs creates a resource profile tailored for distributed parallel workloads rather than single-threaded tasks. Because local storage is absent, external network storage solutions are required for persistent disk space. This instance architecture is suitable for deep learning inference, parallel video encoding, concurrent microservices, and high-throughput batch execution.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated x86_64 server designed for parallel compute and inference workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, it exposes 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores paired with 372.0 GB of RAM. Hardware acceleration is provided by four NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs with a combined 64 GB of VRAM. The instance features a 30 Gbps baseline network connection and lacks local storage. Benchmarks highlight strong multi-threaded execution, achieving 70574.45 in multi-core stress-ng testing and 64.27 million Redis SET operations per second, despite relatively weak single-core metrics. The hardware density makes this instance well matched for multi-GPU machine learning inference, parallel data processing, high-concurrency web microservices, and media transcoding pipelines relying on external storage volumes.
